problem.title: Five Moves from Twenty
problem.statement: A display starts at 20. On each of exactly five moves, a player either adds 4 or subtracts 2. Which number could be the final display?
hints: Track whether the display is odd or even after each allowed move.
After using parity to eliminate, construct five moves to the remaining choice.

solutionSteps.title: Track parity
solutionSteps.body: The display begins even. Adding 4 or subtracting 2 preserves evenness, so every reachable final display is even.

solutionSteps.title: Verify the survivor
solutionSteps.body: Only 22 is even among the choices, and it is reachable: 20 + 4 + 4 − 2 − 2 − 2 = 22.

validationMethods: parity invariant eliminates all four odd choices
independent enumeration by number a of add-four moves gives final 10 + 6a for a from 0 through 5
explicit five-move construction to 22 and answer-choice audit
notes: The reachable set is {10,16,22,28,34,40}; 22 is the sole offered member.

problem.title: Five Odd Addends
problem.statement: Five odd integers are added. What must be the parity of their sum?
hints: Pair four of the odd addends.

solutionSteps.title: Pair the terms
solutionSteps.body: Two pairs of odd integers each have even sums. Adding the fifth odd integer to those even totals gives an odd sum.

validationMethods: pairing proof reduces five odd addends to even plus even plus odd
independent residue calculation 1+1+1+1+1 is congruent to 1 modulo 2
notes: Any sum of an odd number of odd integers is odd.

problem.title: Two Even Changes
problem.statement: A display starts at 18. On each of exactly two moves, a player either adds 6 or subtracts 4. Which number could be the final display?
hints: Check whether the remaining even choice has a two-move route.

solutionSteps.title: Use parity
solutionSteps.body: Starting even and adding or subtracting an even number keeps the display even, so only 20 can work among the choices.

solutionSteps.title: Construct a route
solutionSteps.body: The route 18 + 6 − 4 = 20 uses exactly two moves.

validationMethods: parity invariant eliminates four odd choices
independent enumeration of the four move sequences gives endpoints 30, 20, 20, and 10
notes: 20 is the only offered reachable endpoint.

problem.title: Seventeen Color Switches
problem.statement: A token begins on its black side. Each move flips it to the opposite color, black to white or white to black. What color shows after exactly 17 moves?
hints: Two moves return the token to its starting color.

solutionSteps.title: Use the two-step cycle
solutionSteps.body: Eight pairs of moves return the token to black after 16 moves. The seventeenth move flips it to white.

validationMethods: pairing 16 moves into eight full black-white-black cycles
independent parity-of-move-count rule: odd flips reverse the starting color
notes: The final color is uniquely white.

problem.title: Counters Between Two Boxes
problem.statement: Two boxes begin with 4 and 9 counters. Each move transfers exactly 3 counters from one box to the other, and a move is allowed only when the giving box has at least 3 counters. Which pair of box counts is impossible after any number of moves?
hints: What happens to the total number of counters during a transfer?
Check the sum in each offered pair.

solutionSteps.title: Find the invariant
solutionSteps.body: The boxes begin with 4 + 9 = 13 counters. Every move adds 3 to one box and subtracts 3 from the other, so the total stays 13.

solutionSteps.title: Compare choices
solutionSteps.body: Choices A-D total 13 and are reached by repeated transfers. Choice E totals 14, so it is impossible.

validationMethods: conserved-total proof fixes every reachable sum at 13
independent enumeration of reachable states (1,12), (4,9), (7,6), (10,3), and (13,0)
notes: (8,6) is uniquely impossible because its total is 14.

problem.title: Flip Exactly Two Coins
problem.statement: Six coins begin with tails showing. On each move, exactly two coins are flipped. Which number of heads is impossible after any number of moves?
hints: The two selected coins are TT, HT, or HH before a move.
Find the change in the head count in each case.

solutionSteps.title: Classify one move
solutionSteps.body: Flipping TT changes the head count by +2, flipping one head and one tail changes it by 0, and flipping HH changes it by −2.

solutionSteps.title: Use the invariant
solutionSteps.body: The count starts at 0 and changes only by even amounts, so it always remains even. Three heads is impossible; 0, 2, 4, and 6 are all constructible.

validationMethods: case proof that every move changes head count by -2, 0, or 2
independent construction of 0, 2, 4, and 6 heads and parity exclusion of 3
notes: Three is the only odd choice and therefore the unique impossible head count.
